New Halfa and Wedel Helew localities

OUTPUT 1.1: Agricultural and livestock production of 63,500 vulnerable households (including IDPs, refugees, and host communities) increased through access to inputs, livestock vaccination, climate-smart production, and post-harvest technologies.
Number of smallholder farmers who received improved agriculture inputs and land, disaggregated by sex and age.

UNDP exceeded the target due to the increased demand for agro-inputs among farmers, particularly the youth. This necessity prompted UNDP to respond to the need and provide agro-inputs to enable farmers to go into food production.
Number of target households with increased area under sustainable agriculture production disaggregated by sex and age.

UNDP supported smallholder farmers by providing improved certified seeds and other agro-inputs. UNDP exceeded its targets due to the increased number of smallholder farmers who benefited from these improved agro-inputs. The main farming season starts from May-October and therefore more farmers have targeted and will continue to be the case in the next reporting period as well.
Number of smallholder farmers trained and or educated on new/improved agriculture techniques and technologies.

UNDP deployed Field Extension Officers to facilitate the delivery of extension services to 9,177 smallholder farmers through the establishment of farmer field schools, promoting the adoption of new, improved, and sustainable agricultural production methods. UNDP exceeded the target due to the number of farmers who received improved agro-inputs, who need to acquire Good Agricultural Practices to enhance productivity.
Number of households who received livestock support including restocking and vaccination services, disaggregated by sex and age

UNDP distributed 200 goats (150 milking and 50 male) to 100 vulnerable households. The UNDP was unable to achieve its target due to delays in securing improved breeds. UNDP has addressed this challenge to ensure the distribution of the improved livestock to vulnerable households in Q3 and Q4.
OUTPUT 1.2: Access of 30,000 vulnerable households to socioeconomic productive assets and infrastructure increased
Number and type of water resources rehabilitated and functional.

UNDP has initiated the procurement process to rehabilitate 10 water yards. The tender documents have been finalized. First tranche was completely consumed and due to that, the procurement did not conclude. This was also presented during the monthly meeting. However, UNDP has advanced its core resources to finalize the procurement process and issuing a purchase order.
Number of community warehouses constructed and functioning
Procurement initiated for five (5) warehouses. Due to unavailability of fund the procurement process did not concluded and it was also highlighted in the monthly meeting.
Number of solar cooking stoves provided to communities.
Due to the availability of fund, this could not proceeded.
Number of  farm machinery provided to support agricultural production.
The procurement of 10 tractors and accessories has been completed while using UNDP core resources. The tractors are yet to be delivered and will be reported in next reporting period.
OUTPUT 1.3: Local communities and civil society empowered to promote livelihood and economic recovery enhanced.
Number of Community Management Committees (CMCs) established and functional

UNDP established 14  CMCs, comprising a total membership of 410 individuals. UNDP established the CMCs to oversee the effective management and maintenance of assets provided by the project, including tractors and water yards. UNDP exceeded the target due to the need to ensure the presence of CMCs in targeted communities prior to the delivery of any assets.
Number of  CMCs trained on community mobilization skills and social cohesion promotion
UNDP trained all 14 CMCs that were established. The project exceeded its target due to the need to ensure the presence of CMCs in all communities where the project provided/ will provide assets.
Number of social forums and peace events organised

UNDP organized one (1) social event, involving five (5) youth groups (established by the project), comprising 125 members (50 women and 75 men), to promote peaceful co-existence. UNDP was unable to meet the target because the timing of the activities coincided with the farming season. The project will organize the events after the farming season.

OUTPUT 2.1: Income-generating and labor-intensive employment opportunities created for 4,500 vulnerable households.
Number of Voluntary Savings and Loans Associations (VSLAs) established that are functional.

UNDP was unable to meet the target because the timing of the activities coincided with the farming season. The beneficiaries are engaged in farming business during the rainy season. UNDP will establish the VSLAs in Q4.
Number of micro-grants provided disaggregated by types of enterprises and sex of owners.

UNDP was unable to meet the target. The beneficiaries also engage in off-season agribusiness enterprises, and they will only need grants after the agricultural production. Providing microcredit at this time will not yield the expected outcome. UNDP will provide the micro-grants to the beneficiaries in Q4, when they need to purchase agricultural commodities.
Number of  young people participating in Cash for Work activities disagregated by gender and by age group.

UNDP facilitated temporary employment opportunities through its Cash for Work initiative in Gedaref and the River Nile states, engaging a total of 275 individuals. However, UNDP was unable to meet its target due to the need for the youth to engage in their own farming activities. The Cash for Work activities will resume soon after the farming season.
OUTPUT 2.2: Linkages and access to markets facilitated for 1,700 smallholder producers, associations and enterprises.
Number of target beneficiaries trained on market access strategies disagregated by sex and age.
UNDP postponed the training sessions for Q3 and Q4 to allow farmers to fully engage in their crucial farming activities during the peak season.
